jobs.title: Store Manager
jobs.desc:
Top Oil is recruiting for a Store Manager to join our store in Ballyvolane, Co. Cork.
Here's what you can expect from us:
When you're a part of our team, you'll see how we bring good energy to our business and our employees. Across the markets we serve, our teams share the value that people matter – employees, customers and community. Every day, we strive to make a difference in the places we serve and the communities we call home. It is an important part of who we are as a company and something we all work hard to do every day. Our collaborative approach, commitment to diversity and inclusion along with our safety-first culture helps reinforce our internal brand position where People Matter. That's why we're dedicated to the development of our employees, so that they can reach their career goals.
What will your day look like?
As a Store Manager you will be responsible for managing all aspects of the service operation in our retail store. You will ensure the store operates efficiently and effectively and be responsible for motivating and invigorating all of your employees to provide our customers with the beststore experience, fresh food offerings and customer service at all times, thus hitting key store targets. You will also promote positive culture of a proactive approach to all HSE rules and regulations, with a safety first mind-set in everything we do.
Your Responsibilities:
• To oversee and ensure the smooth running of the stores.
• You will work collaboratively with your Regional Store Manager in setting, monitoring and achieving the sales targets set out with the team on gross profit margin, net margin, waste and other KPIs.
• You will insure all new employees are inducted and trained to the highest standards in all aspects of their role, in accordance with policies, procedures and best practice of the company;
• You will be responsible for ensuring security and health and safety standards upheld, protecting customers and employees through providing a safe store environment during COVID19 and thereafter.
• You will be encouraging Staff to engage in upselling promotional offers and helping to train staff to identify opportunities to upsell and how to do so.
• Stock Control Management is a key part to your position and managing all process around this in line with our company standards is essential.
• You will manage all aspects of your employee rostering, annual leave while practicing good GDPR measures with these records in line with our GDPR policy.
• Ensure merchandising and presentation of entire store is always of the highest standard and in accordance with relevant store planograms and guidelines ensuring government guidelines of social distancing are adhered to.
• You will be engaging with new initiatives and embrace new ways of working with a positive can-do attitude and you will thrive to do this with you lead by example attitude.
What we look for in you:
We want you to thrive within our organisation and experience has shown us that the best managers are highly driven with a strong work ethic, who lead their team by example, and who are superb under pressure at maintaining and promoting a happy, safe and inclusive work environment.
With these personal attributes you will also have:
• Ideally a minimum of 2-3 years` experience in a dynamic retail management position.
• Proven skills managing people and communicating effectively
• A proven track record of hitting KPIs / targets.
• Hands on exposure to stock management, financial management & reporting systems.
• Strong knowledge and experience of reading and actioning reports.
• Good knowledge of Microsoft Office (Excel, Word).
Top Oil supports a diverse and inclusive work environment and welcomes applications from all qualified applicant

jobs.title: Principal Industrial Designer
jobs.desc:
Logitech is the Sweet Spot for people who want their actions to have a positive global impact while having the flexibility to do it in their own way.
Principal Industrial Designer - Mouse Design Team : Cork, Ireland
Hybrid role - base 3 days a week on site*
THE ROLE
Logitech is seeking a Principal Industrial Designer to join our Mouse Design Team in Cork. This is a senior-level position for a recognised expert who balances world-class craft with strategic foresight — a thinker and a doer. You will work on complex design assignments, solving unique challenges that have a broad impact on our product portfolio and the future direction of our businesses.
Based in our Cork office, you will be a key member of a team dedicated to excellence in handheld products, leading the creation of mice that are as comfortable, ergonomically superior as they are visually groundbreaking.
WHY IS THIS ROLE IMPORTANT FOR LOGITECH?
The mouse is at the core of Logitech's product portfolio. We design the tools people reach for every day - products where form, material, ergonomics, and engineering precision must coexist seamlessly and where world class design quality is non-negotiable. At the Principal level, you will be shaping the future of one of our most competitive and scrutinised product categories. We prototype to learn, design to inspire, and ship real products that people enthuse about and love to use.
YOUR CONTRIBUTION
Move fast. Speak up. Decide and own. Drive change.
Visionary Craft & Innovation: Lead the design and development of future-forward mouse experiences, transforming complex human problems into polished, intuitive, and beautiful design solutions.
Strategic Influence: Partner with senior leadership to shape the long-term direction of the Mouse Design Team, ensuring design strategy aligns with emerging trends and business objectives.
Design Excellence: Manage key design processes and projects from brief through to production builds, maintaining an unrelenting focus on quality, detail, and creative confidence.
Mentorship & Leadership: Provide guidance and thought leadership to the broader design team. Mentor other designers and foster a culture of curiosity and exceptional craftsmanship.
Collaborative Networking: Build strong relationships with engineering, product marketing, and business stakeholders to drive design quality and change across a multidisciplinary environment.
Key Qualifications
To be considered, you must bring the following minimum skills and behaviours to our team:
Proven Track Record: 10+ years of relevant experience in Industrial Design, either in-house or at a leading agency, with a portfolio of successful, high-volume consumer hardware products.
Physical-Digital Mastery: Exceptional hands-on skills in sketching, visualisation, and physical prototyping (including hand-sculpting in foam). Deep understanding of anthropometrics, ergonomics, and the iterative digital-to-physical workflow required for handheld devices.
3D CAD Mastery: Expert-level proficiency in surface CAD - excellent working knowledge of Rhino, SolidWorks, Alias, Fusion or Creo Parametric, Class-A surfacing principles and experience exchanging high-quality 3D files with mechanical engineers and CAD specialists.
CMF & Manufacturing: Working expertise in Materials, Colours and Finishes, Design for Manufacturing, and EVT/DVT/PVT build processes — you understand how to maintain design intent through engineering development.
AI Proficiency: Comfortable integrating AI tools (e.g., Vizcom, Gemini, Magnific) into ideation and concept visualisation workflows. Able to move faster and explore more broadly because of it - not instead of core craft.
Communication & Storytelling: Able to craft compelling design narratives and present persuasively to stakeholders at all levels, from engineers to senior executives.
Highly driven, collaborative, and a proactive self-starter — you take on ambiguous assignments and drive them through to valuable outcomes.
Education: Bachelor's degree or higher in Industrial Design, Product Design, or a related field.
OUR CULTURE
At Logitech, we act like a small company. We believe that anyone can have the best idea. We value designers who are humble, hungry, and brave enough to challenge conventional thinking — and we offer a highly collaborative, international environment where your work will impact millions of people worldwide.
Logitech is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. Individuals seeking employment at Logitech are considered without regard to race, colour, religion, national origin, age, sex, marital status, ancestry, physical or mental disability, veteran status, or sexual orientation.
Across Logitech we empower collaboration and foster play. We help teams collaborate/learn from anywhere, without compromising on productivity or continuity so it should be no surprise that most of our jobs are open to work from home from most locations. Our hybrid work model allows some employees to work remotely while others work on-premises. Within this structure, you may have teams or departments split between working remotely and working in-house.
Logitech is an amazing place to work because it is full of authentic people who are inclusive by nature as well as by design. Being a global company, we value our diversity and celebrate all our differences. Don’t meet every single requirement? Not a problem. If you feel you are the right candidate for the opportunity, we strongly recommend that you apply. We want to meet you!
We offer comprehensive and competitive benefits packages and working environments that are designed to be flexible and help you to care for yourself and your loved ones, now and in the future. We believe that good health means more than getting medical care when you need it. Logitech supports a culture that encourages individuals to achieve good physical, financial, emotional, intellectual and social wellbeing so we all can create, achieve and enjoy more and support our families. We can’t wait to tell you more about them being that there are too many to list here and they vary based on location.
All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, sex, age, color, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, protected veteran status, or on the basis of disability.
If you require an accommodation to complete any part of the application process, are limited in the ability, are unable to access or use this online application process and need an alternative method for applying, you may contact us toll free at +1-510-713-4866 for assistance and we will get back to you as soon as possible.

jobs.title: Management Accountant
jobs.desc:
Management Accountant
My client is looking for an experienced Management Accountant
to join their finance team and take responsibility for the financial performance of a key operational division.
Reporting to the Financial Controller, you will work closely with senior management and operational teams, providing financial insight and helping to drive performance, cost control and profitability.
Key Responsibilities
Manage financial reporting and performance for the assigned business area.
Lead budgeting, forecasting and regular P&L reporting.
Analyse financial results, investigate variances and identify opportunities for improvement.
Partner with operational managers to manage costs and deliver against budgets.
Provide financial support for tenders, pricing and commercial decisions.
Lead regular financial performance reviews with senior stakeholders.
Support the wider finance team with group reporting and management accounts.
Produce financial analysis and ad hoc reports as required.
About You
Professionally qualified accountant with 5 years’ post-qualification experience.
Strong commercial awareness and analytical ability.
Confident influencing and partnering with senior stakeholders.
Excellent communication and presentation skills.
Self-motivated, organised and comfortable working independently.
Adaptable, reliable and able to manage competing priorities.
Willing to travel between company locations when required.
What's on Offer?
Hybrid working available following an initial six-month period.
Competitive Salary
A commercially focused role with direct exposure to senior leadership and operational decision-making.

jobs.title: Customer Assistant - Ballincollig Express
jobs.desc:
About the role
We pride ourselves on offering customers the biggest range of products around. And that's not just food, but everything from clothes and kettles to financial services.
But did you know we offer the biggest job opportunities too? With stores across the UK and Ireland, and a variety of roles, we are always looking for people who are as passionate about helping customers as we are.
Our Every Little Helps approach doesn't just apply to our customers. It's at the very heart of everything we do at work - and it's what makes us different. We believe in treating each other with respect, and everyone having the opportunity to get on. That's what makes Tesco such a great place to work.
Should you be successful in your application, your offer will be subject to and conditional upon you providing your bank account details before your agreed start date.
You will be responsible for
Always put the customer first and consider them in everything you do.
Get to know your customers and serve them with pride.
Help to ensure products and services are available for customers at all times.
Handle all products with care to maintain quality and ensure they reach the customer in the best condition.
Keep the shop floor and back areas clean and tidy at all times.
Using the training you receive, follow department routines and processes.
Follow all company policies and adhere to Health and Safety routines.
Whilst you will have a core role, you may be asked to support your colleagues by helping in other departments.
You will need
Able to give great, natural customer service by proactively smiling, greeting, acknowledging and helping customers.
Works hard for customers, your team and your department.
You are able to prioritise to ensure anything you do is right for our customers.
Adaptable and resilient to meet the ever changing demands of our business.
You must be able to follow instructions either verbal or written.
You are reliable and a good timekeeper.
You must be smart and tidy at all times.
Whats in it for you?
We offer excellent benefits that help make Tesco a great place to work. These include but aren't limited to:
Competitive Salary
Bonus Scheme*
Our Virtual GP service provides free and confidential access to an online GP through video GP consultations, and online prescription service for colleagues. The service is also available to families of colleagues who live at the same address for a reduced cost.
24/7 access to our Employee Assistance Programme (EAP) for you and family members for in the moment emotional support along with free access to a range of wellbeing services supporting you under our new Wellbeing First approach of Body, Mind and Life.
Colleague Clubcard offering 10% discount across stores and online, with 15% discount weekends once a month (Friday to Sunday), and 20% off twice a year. There is also 20% off F&F clothing, all year long, these various discounts can be extended to a family member with a 2nd Clubcard available.*
Life Assurance
Pension Plan*
Save As You Earn Scheme*
Paid Family Leave
Bike to Work
Long Service Awards
Commuter Scheme
*Entry requirements and rules of the scheme apply
About Us
Our vision at Tesco is to become every customer's favourite way to shop, whether they are at home or out on the move. Our core purpose is "Serving our customers, communities and planet a little better every day". Serving means more than a transactional relationship with our customers. It means acting as a responsible and sustainable business for all stakeholders, for the communities we are part of, and for the planet. Through initiatives like the Tesco Community Fund, our association with Children's Health Foundation, our partnership with FoodCloud and our Stronger Starts programme, we have supported over 21,000 community groups, raised over €7.5 million for medical equipment, and provided almost 15 million meals nationwide, to those living in food insecurity.
Tesco has operated in the Irish retail market since 1997, and with 190+ stores nationwide, we employ over 13,000 people in cities and towns around Ireland, supporting almost 45,000 jobs directly and indirectly. We partner with over 500 Irish suppliers - of which almost three-quarters are small and medium enterprises - which in turn supports almost 13,000 farming families around Ireland. Tesco is the single largest buyer of Irish food and drink in the world, buying €1.6 Billion a year; more than any other single country in the European Union, more than even the USA which you perceive as a massive buyer of Irish food.
We work closely with suppliers across Ireland who are dedicated to making the best products for our customers and this is reflected in the numerous awards our products have won over the years including Blás Na hÉireann, World Steak Challenge and Great Taste Awards.
We are proud to have an inclusive culture at Tesco where everyone truly feels able to be themselves. It is embedded in our values: we treat people how they want to be treated. At Tesco, we not only celebrate diversity, but recognise the value and opportunity it brings. We always want our colleagues to feel they can be themselves at work and we are committed to helping them be at their best.
We know life looks a little different for each of us. That's why at Tesco, we always welcome chats about flexible working. Some people are at the start of their careers, some want the freedom to do the things they love. Others are going through life-changing moments like becoming a carer, nearing retirement, adapting to parenthood, or something else. So, talk to us throughout your application about how we can support.
Tesco is committed to celebrating diversity and everyone is welcome at Tesco. We're committed to providing a fully inclusive recruitment process, allowing candidates the opportunity to thrive and inform us of any reasonable adjustments they may require. For further information on the accessibility support we can offer, please click http://roi.tesco-careers.com/accessibility/
How can I let Tesco know I need additional support?
Please let us know you need additional support by emailing tescoireland.recruitment@tesco.ie
This will allow us to understand more about you and how we can best support you through the recruitment process.

jobs.title: SALES ASSISTANT - FULL TIME - WILTON
jobs.desc:

jobs.title: Night Porter
jobs.desc:
DEPARTMENT/LOCATION
: Front of House
PURPOSE OF JOB:
To ensure that guest queries/needs are quickly and effectively met at night. Ensure that regular security checks and fire checks are carried out each night. To carry out a comprehensive night audit.
RESPONSIBLE TO:
Duty Managers
RESPONSIBLE FOR:
Responsible for the supervision and operations of premises at night.
Duties
MAIN DUTIES:
To arrive for work on time dressed neatly in a full clean uniform, well-groomed, with a name badge and presenting a professional appearance to our guests.
Receive a full handover from the a) Daily Porters b) Receptionists on duty c) Manager on duty
Complete docket checks as appropriate and inform the early Duty Manager of any discrepancies.
Carry out security/fire checks at regular intervals (i.e. 12 am, 2 am, 4 am and 6 am) or as required and log any irregularities in the Handover book, reporting it to the Duty Manager.
To efficiently check-in/out guests during hours of duty and ensure their luggage is brought/collected quickly.
To deal with any guest enquiries/needs quickly and effectively.
To carry out any Lounge/Room Service Orders required after 11 pm to an agreed standard. The kitchen and food preparation areas must be maintained in a clean manner.
To collect Breakfast cards while doing floor checks and prepare and deliver Room Service.
Ensure that any early breakfasts are delivered to the guest on time and to standard.
To cover Bar Service once bar staff has left ensuring correct and diligent cash and stock procedures.
To carry out cleaning as per the night cleaning schedule.
Cleaning of public areas as assigned by management.
Maintenance of Premier Lounge. Stock replenished as required.
Reception desk and office cleaned.
Ensure meeting rooms are refreshed and prepared.
Cleaning of public bathroom areas.
Ensure front areas of the hotel are tidy, cleared of debris and clean.
If necessary, set up meeting rooms to the agreed standard, checking that all equipment is correct and in working order.
To check the fax machine on a regular basis and ensure guests receive any faxes or other messages quickly.
Complete full report of night shift events in diary and handover any problems/incidents to a) Duty Manager b) Receptionist c) Day Porter on duty prior to leaving.
Additional and reasonable duties may be assigned as deemed appropriate by management.

Protea Recruitment is working with an established food manufacturing business in West Cork to recruit a Warehouse Controller for its newly built warehouse facility.

Take responsibility for the day-to-day operation of the frozen cold store and ambient packaging warehouse.
Oversee the receipt, checking, storage and movement of raw materials, packaging and finished goods.

Previous experience in warehouse operations, stock control or inventory management.

Strong understanding of stock management, stock rotation and inventory accuracy.
Confident IT skills, including experience using warehouse or stock management systems.
Ability to work independently, prioritise tasks and take ownership of daily operations.
Excellent attention to detail and organisational skills.
A strong commitment to workplace safety and operational standards.
Desirable:
Experience within food manufacturing, chilled/frozen food distribution or FMCG.

Competitive salary dependent on experience and accomodation.

jobs.title: Quality Engineer
jobs.desc:
Quality Engineer
Location: Cork, Ireland
Duration: 12 month Contract
Hours: 39
Imagine your next project utilising Quality Engineering tools and principles across the complete product lifecycle to support medical devices and diagnostics that impact patients worldwide.
Global Services, LLC., represents more than 60 manufacturing sites and 26,000 employees who plan, source, manufacture and deliver high-quality and cost-effective medical products to our customers around the globe each day. Work of the MD&D Supply Chain supports a multitude of product platforms, new products and delivery systems that are used in a wide range of procedures throughout the healthcare industry, including interventional cardiology, electrophysiology, minimally invasive surgery, hospital sterilization, clinical laboratory testing, diabetes management, joint replacement surgery and vision care.
The Quality Engineer conducts assignments encompassing complete projects or portions of major projects and determines methods and techniques to be used or adapts standard methods to meet variations. The Quality Engineer utilises Quality Engineering tools and practices for the effective and efficient development, transfer, and maintenance of products/processes throughout the product lifecycle and Quality Engineering principles and problem-solving skills to improve and maintain products/processes that are aligned with the overall Quality and Business vision. They utilise appropriate risk management to prevent unanticipated failure modes and improve capability of processes.
This position acts in accordance with all applicable federal, state and local laws/regulations and Corporate Johnson & Johnson procedures and guidelines. The role reports to the Quality Engineering Leader and partners with R&D and other cross-functional partners to ensure the proper application of design controls, NPI design transfer risk management and the investigation/correction of design failures/challenges. Additionally, this position partners with Global Supply Chain, finished goods and material suppliers to ensure appropriate application of process validation, process control, and risk management; and the investigation/correction of process failures when needed.
roles and responsibilities
Support Continuous Improvement, Quality Assurance and Performance through Lean, Six Sigma, Kaizen, PDCA.
Collect data and execute/conduct various analytical/statistical analyses and interpretation as part of process improvements and day-to-day support.
Review the effectiveness of continuous improvement tools and techniques; conduct benchmarking to develop more effective methods for improving quality.
Implement and review effectiveness of Non-Conformance Reporting and CAPA.
Analyse/review current product and processes are in compliance to ISO 13485, QSR etc., and champion compliance to global regulations such as FDA, MDR, support internal and external audits.
Conduct periodic line audits for compliance to production controls and review audit findings for NonConformance and CAPA.
Support activities in material review board, material identification, segregation, and defect classification.
Initiate escalation for non-conformance, implement immediate corrective actions and conduct investigation, root cause analysis and bounding of non-conformance as per established process.
Develop, interpret, and implement appropriate process monitoring and control methods consistent with the level of process/product risk.
Develop, interpret, and implement standard and non-standard sampling plans.
Assess effectiveness of measurement tools, destructive tests, non-destructive tests, measurement system analysis.
Assess and interpret common versus special cause variation in manufacturing processing and determine adequacy of current process limits.
Conduct failure modes cause analysis for products and processes.
Document, justify, review, or analyse whether a proposed change to a process will not enhance the risk level in some way beyond capability of current controls or whether change will result in potential noncompliance to a required standard.
Assess the need for risk mitigation techniques given product classification, potential defect types, defect frequency, severity, patient risk, process capability, process controls, etc.
Determine effectiveness of these techniques on previously implemented improvements.
Conduct, review, and approve IQ, OQ/PQ and CSV for manufacturing and test equipment.
Establishes suitable measurement systems through the principles of MSA for the collection and analysis of unbiased, reliable, and consistent data e.g., Gauge Repeatability and Reproducibility.
Analyzes and reviews sources of variation in measurement systems, with a view to control of variation.
Ensures effective quality strategies are created for the validation of test methods, process, and design.
how to succeed
A minimum of a bachelor’s degree, preferably in Engineering or related technical field.
2-4 years’ experience in a related position.
Experience working in both an FDA and European regulatory environment is preferred
Requires relevant experience working in manufacturing/operations.
Experience with a proven track record of implementing appropriate risk mitigation.
Technical training and experience using Statistics, Lean and Six Sigma Methodologies is preferred, i.e., Measurement System Analysis, SPC, DOEs, Reliability, etc.
Strong knowledge of statistical software packages is preferred and ability to preview, graph and analyze data and be able to present data that facilitates/drives decision making.
Ability to perform "hands on" troubleshooting and problem solving is preferred, to think on their feet and providing sound judgment is highly desired.
Good technical understanding of manufacturing equipment and processes is required.
Understanding of the NPI (New Product Introduction) process and Process Validation expertise is preferred.
A thorough understanding of GMP/ISO regulations for validation and product/process Risk Management (FDA and ISO standards) is preferred.
benefits
This role offers a very competitive hourly rate. This contract will run for 12 months

jobs.desc:
Our kitchen only works well when it’s clean, organised and ready for the day.
As a Kitchen Assistant, you’ll play a big part in keeping everything running smoothly, from cleaning equipment and work areas to keeping things organised, supporting prep and making sure the kitchen is always safe and ready for the team.

What You’ll Do
Keep the kitchen spotless
Clean and sanitise work surfaces, floors, sinks, equipment and utensils throughout the day so the kitchen stays safe and ready to use.
Look after equipment
Clean kitchen equipment properly, follow the correct cleaning procedures and help make sure everything is stored safely and where it should be.
Keep things organised
Make sure the kitchen is tidy, stock is stored correctly and work areas stay clear and organised throughout the shift.
Support the prep team
If you have time outside of cleaning, you can help with basic food prep, washing and preparing ingredients, and getting the kitchen set up for the day.
Stay on top of cleaning
Work through cleaning checklists, spot jobs that need doing and take action rather than waiting to be asked.
Keep food and people safe
Follow food safety, allergen, hygiene and health & safety procedures carefully at all times.
Jump in when it gets busy
Support the wider kitchen and restaurant team wherever needed, especially during busy periods.
You’ll probably love being a Kitchen Assistant at Sprout if...
You take real pride in keeping things clean and organised
You notice when something needs doing and get on with it
You don’t mind getting stuck into the less glamorous jobs
You like being busy and working as part of a team
You’re reliable and someone people can count on
You care about doing things properly and safely
You’re curious and happy to learn new skills
You like the idea of growing into other kitchen roles over time
If you’re looking for a role where cleaning is someone else’s job or where you can leave things for the next shift, this probably isn’t the one.
A Little About Experience
You don’t need previous kitchen experience, we’ll teach you everything you need to know.
What matters most is that you’re willing to learn, comfortable with physical and hands-on work, and genuinely take pride in keeping the kitchen clean, safe and organised.
If that sounds like you, we’d love to hear from you.

jobs.title: Production Planner
jobs.desc:
About Munters
Munters is a global leader in climate solutions for mission-critical processes. Through innovative and energy-efficient technologies, we enable customers across industries to control humidity, temperature, and energy use efficiently. Together, we support our customers in optimizing performance while contributing to a healthier planet.
With more than 70 years of experience, Munters serves industries such as Data Centers, Battery production, Food, Pharma, and Manufacturing worldwide. We combine innovation, sustainability, and engineering expertise to create solutions that make a real difference for both our customers and the environment.
At Munters, you will be part of a collaborative and international organization where continuous improvement, knowledge sharing, and personal growth are encouraged. Come as you are and be part of our journey.
Main Areas Of Responsibilities
Production Planning and Scheduling
Develop and maintain production schedules that align with customer demand, sales forecasts, and manufacturing capacity. This involves analysing customer orders, sales projections, and manufacturing capabilities to create detailed production plans that outline the sequence and timing of production activities.
Analyse production requirements, material availability, and labour resources to optimize production planning. This involves assessing the materials, components, and labour needed for each product, identifying potential constraints, and adjusting the production schedule to ensure efficient resource utilization and timely order fulfilment.
Schedule production activities to ensure smooth flow of materials, efficient resource utilization, and timely completion of orders. This involves breaking down production processes into individual tasks, assigning tasks to specific workstations or teams, and coordinating the movement of materials and components throughout the production process.
Production Process Optimization
Analyse production processes to identify areas for improvement, potential bottlenecks, and waste reduction opportunities. This involves conducting detailed process reviews, collecting data on process performance, and identifying areas where efficiency can be enhanced, lead times can be reduced, and costs can be minimized.
Implement process improvements to enhance efficiency, reduce lead times, and minimize production costs. This involves developing and implementing process changes, such as streamlining workflows, introducing new technologies, or adopting lean manufacturing principles, to achieve operational excellence.
Collaborate with engineering and operations teams to optimize production processes and ensure adherence to quality standards. This involves working closely with engineering teams to design and implement process improvements, and collaborating with operations teams to ensure that new processes are effectively implemented and monitored for adherence to quality standards.
You will also be expected to carry out any additional duties that may be assigned to you by the company from time to time.

jobs.title: Solutions Engineer, EMEA
jobs.desc:
About Nooks.ai
Nooks is an applied AI lab building the Agent Workspace for GTM. We design AI agents that operate across the full sales action set, from
account strategy
to
prospect research
and
outreach
. Building 0→1 has never been easier, but selling at the speed of the market remains the last frontier for AI. Our mission is to 10x every seller by automating the busywork so they can focus on what humans do best: closing deals.
Today, over 1,500 customers run on Nooks, including Notion, HubSpot, Cursor, and Rippling. We’ve raised $70M+ from top VCs like Kleiner Perkins, which made its first sales-tech investment in over a decade with us. Since then, we’ve tripled ARR each year for 3 years running and grown a high-caliber team turning the art of sales into a scalable science.
Title:
Founding Solutions Engineer (EMEA)
Location:
Primary: Dublin; secondary: Remote, UK or Ireland
About The Role
Nooks is the Agent Workspace for Sales, where reps and AI agents don’t just execute tasks, they decide next moves, with intelligence that compounds over time. We’re growing fast (4x YoY since Series B), our customers spend 4+ hours a day inside Nooks, and the SE function is one of the highest-leverage bets in the business: SE-supported deals close at nearly 6x the rate of unsupported ones.
As our
first Solutions Engineer in EMEA
, you’ll partner with the founding EMEA GTM team to build the territory and establish how we win technically in the region. You’ll own technical discovery, demos, and trial strategy while building the processes, tools, and customer experiences that make the motion repeatable.
You’ll have an established global SE foundation to build on, alongside substantial ownership of what needs to work differently in EMEA. That means adapting our playbook to regional buying processes, creating new approaches where needed, and turning early customer learning into a stronger sales motion.
We’re looking for someone who enjoys both winning deals and building the systems behind them. If you’re a seller who thinks like an engineer, or an engineer who’s found their competitive edge in the deal, this is built for you.
What You'll Do
Own the technical win across EMEA: Lead the full technical sales lifecycle across concurrent opportunities, from discovery and demo through trial and close, with a clear mandate to drive each to a decision.
Build the territory with the founding EMEA GTM team: Partner with AEs and regional leadership on account strategy, customer engagement, and the technical approach needed to create and win early opportunities.
Create an EMEA-specific SE motion: Adapt and build discovery frameworks, demo narratives, trial plans, success criteria, and handoffs that reflect regional customer needs and buying processes.
Connect technical discovery to business outcomes: Get underneath feature requests to uncover real business pain, then build a solution narrative tied to executive priorities and measurable value.
Lead prospect trials: Serve as the primary technical contact, establish clear evaluation plans, monitor trial health, flag risks early, and intervene before issues threaten the deal.
Navigate complex evaluations: Coordinate with internal experts on integrations, security, data handling, and procurement requirements, keeping customers aligned on a credible path forward.
Build the regional operating foundation: Create reusable assets, document what works, and introduce automation that helps a small team cover more opportunities effectively.
Connect the EMEA field to Product: Translate recurring customer needs, competitive insights, and trial patterns into actionable feedback for Product and the global SE team.
Help shape future SE growth in EMEA: Codify the regional playbook and contribute to onboarding and developing future teammates as the business grows.
What You Bring
Prior experience in a quota-carrying or technical sales role, such as AE, SE, or hybrid, with ownership of the pre-sale cycle.
Experience supporting EMEA customers and navigating regional buying processes, stakeholder dynamics, and technical evaluations.
A builder’s mindset: you can create a process, test it in live deals, and improve it without waiting for a complete playbook.
A sales-first instinct: you treat trials like pipeline, care deeply about win rates, and build urgency around real customer priorities.
The ability to engage senior stakeholders, including CROs, CTOs, and VPs of Sales, and lead discovery or a business review independently.
Technical curiosity and sound reasoning: you understand how systems connect, investigate unfamiliar requirements, and close knowledge gaps independently.
Strong discovery skills: you ask “why is that a requirement?” before answering it and develop a point of view before prescribing a solution.
The judgment to prioritize across active deals and foundational work, knowing when to solve something yourself and when to involve global partners.
A bias toward action and comfort owning ambiguous, undocumented work as the first SE in a new region.
Early regional expansion or founding-team experience is a strong plus, as is familiarity with MEDDIC, MEDDPICC, or an equivalent enterprise sales methodology.
Equal Employment Opportunity Statement
Nooks is an equal opportunity employer committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive workforce. We believe in providing equal employment opportunities to all individuals regardless of race, color, religion, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.
Nooks does not discriminate in hiring, promotion, compensation, or any other employment practices, and we are committed to ensuring a workplace that is free from discrimination, harassment, and retaliation. We encourage individuals from all backgrounds to apply and join our team.

jobs.desc:

Location: Cork
Join Musgrave – A Legacy of Innovation, Community, and Excellence
Musgrave is one of Europe’s most successful family-owned businesses, with a rich 150-year legacy in food and brand innovation. We're proud to serve communities across Ireland and Spain, feeding one in three people every day through 19 iconic brands like SuperValu, Centra, Mace, Frank and Honest, and Musgrave MarketPlace. By supporting thousands of retail and foodservice family businesses, we make a positive impact on the communities they serve. We're committed to becoming the most trusted and sustainable business in Ireland, and we're looking for dynamic, forward-thinking individuals to join us on this journey.
As we continue our journey toward becoming Ireland’s most trusted and sustainable business, we have an exciting opportunity for a successful candidate to join our Financal Control team.
Role Purpose
The Senior Financial Accountant – Northern Ireland is a senior Financial Control role responsible for the financial accounting, control, compliance and reporting agenda supporting the Musgrave Northern Ireland business.
The role owns cashflow forecasting, capital expenditure and depreciation reporting, quarterly HMRC compliance, intercompany governance in an outsourced operating model, and control and assurance reporting including MACSAC.
Working closely with NI Finance, Group Financial Control, Tax, Treasury, the outsourced service provider and External Audit, the role provides accurate reporting, independent challenge and assurance over the NI control environment, while driving standardisation and continuous improvement in line with the Group Financial Control agenda.
What you'll be doing:
Cashflow, Capital Expenditure & Depreciation
Own the preparation, review and challenge of short and medium-term cashflow forecasting for the NI business, including variance analysis against actuals. Including working capital reviews.
Forecast and report capital expenditure and the associated depreciation profile, working with business owners to validate phasing, spend and asset readiness.
Ensure capital spend is appropriately authorised, correctly capitalised and depreciated in line with Group accounting policy.
Provide insight to NI and Group leadership on cash, capex and depreciation trends, risks and opportunities.
Tax & Statutory Compliance (HMRC)
Prepare, review and submit quarterly HMRC returns for the NI entities, ensuring accuracy, completeness and timely filing.
Coordinate the quarterly VAT product file review process, engaging commercial and master data stakeholders to confirm correct VAT treatment and resolve exceptions.
Maintain robust documentation and audit trail supporting all returns and product file decisions.
Work with the Group Tax team on technical queries, legislative change and HMRC correspondence.
Intercompany Oversight & Outsourced Model Governance
Provide oversight and governance of intercompany transactions, balances, reconciliations and settlement across NI and Group entities.
Act as the retained control owner over activities performed by the outsourced service provider, reviewing outputs rather than performing the underlying processing.
Monitor service performance, SLA delivery and escalations, ensuring issues are resolved and root causes addressed.
Ensure intercompany balances are agreed, eliminated correctly on consolidation and supported by clear documentation.
Controls, Assurance & Reporting
Own MACSAC reporting for the NI business, including self-assessment, evidence, scoring and remediation of control gaps.
Ensure period-end controls, balance sheet reconciliations and journals meet Group standards and are reviewed on a timely basis.
Support internal and external audit requests and ensure timely closure of audit and management actions.
Prepare clear control and financial reporting updates for Financial Control forums and senior leadership.
Additional Financial Accounting Activity
Support the acquisition agenda within Retail.
Support lease accounting, including new leases, modifications and related disclosures.
Support insurance accounting, renewals data and related cost allocation.
Review employee expenses for compliance with policy, VAT treatment and control standards.
Support statutory financial statements preparation and audit for the NI entities.
Support wider Group Financial Control, transformation and process improvement initiatives as required.
What we are looking for:
Essential
Qualified Chartered Accountant (or equivalent).
3+ years post-qualified experience in financial accounting, financial control or audit.
Strong technical accounting knowledge and understanding of internal controls and financial governance.
Experience of cashflow forecasting, fixed assets and capital expenditure reporting.
Practical VAT and indirect tax compliance experience, ideally including HMRC filings.
Strong analytical, reconciliation and problem-solving skills with high attention to detail.
Ability to work with and challenge an outsourced service provider in a retained oversight model.
Strong stakeholder management and communication skills across finance and non-finance audiences.
Desirable
Experience in retail, wholesale or FMCG.
Knowledge of UK and Irish tax and statutory reporting requirements.
Experience with Oracle, Onspring, Power BI or similar finance and control systems.
Why Musgrave:
Career Development: With a commitment to your personal and professional growth, Musgrave offers numerous opportunities for advancement and learning.
Collaborative Environment: Work alongside a passionate team, where your contributions will make a significant impact
Innovation Focus: Be part of a company that values forward-thinking solutions
Community Focus: Be part of a company that truly values its communities and strives to make a positive impact.
Be Part of a Legacy: Join a company with a long-standing commitment to community and innovation.
Ready to make an impact?
Apply now and be part of a forward-thinking company that values your expertise and vision.
Musgrave is an equal opportunities employer. We encourage applications from diverse candidates. If we can make any accommodations to enable you to be the best version of yourself during the interview, please let us know.
Musgrave operate a Work Smart hybrid working model where you can alternate your time between connecting and collaborating in the business and working remotely.

jobs.title: Senior BIM Engineer
jobs.desc:
Our client, an established international engineering business specialising in water treatment and critical infrastructure, is seeking a Senior BIM Engineer to join its growing team. Operating across Europe, the company delivers engineering solutions for data centres, pharmaceuticals, power, food and beverage, manufacturing and industrial sectors. The role offers a salary of €60,000–€70,000, depending on experience, alongside career progression, ongoing training, professional development and exposure to complex international engineering projects.
About Your New Employer
Join an established international engineering business specialising in water treatment and critical infrastructure.
Work on projects across data centres, pharmaceuticals, food and beverage, manufacturing and energy.
Gain exposure to international engineering projects from concept and detailed design through to installation and handover.
Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams across different offices and markets.
Benefit from ongoing training, career progression and professional development opportunities.
About Your New Job
As a Senior BIM Engineer, you will lead BIM coordination, model quality assurance and digital delivery across multidisciplinary engineering projects, ensuring models and technical documentation meet project requirements and industry standards.
Your responsibilities will include:
Leading the development, coordination and quality assurance of BIM models using Autodesk Revit.
Coordinating multidisciplinary models, including clash detection, design reviews and constructability assessments.
Ensuring BIM deliverables comply with project requirements, BIM Execution Plans and ISO 19650 principles.
Providing technical guidance and mentorship to BIM Technicians and BIM Engineers.
Developing and maintaining Revit templates, BIM libraries, digital standards and automation workflows.
Managing project information and document exchange through Common Data Environments (CDEs).
Collaborating with project teams to improve digital delivery, model quality and coordination efficiency.
Supporting project planning, resource allocation and BIM implementation throughout the project lifecycle.
What Skills You Need
A degree in Architecture, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Civil Engineering or a related discipline.
A minimum of five years' experience delivering BIM projects.
Strong proficiency in Autodesk Revit and working knowledge of AutoCAD.
Experience leading or mentoring BIM Technicians and Engineers.
Experience with Navisworks, Autodesk Construction Cloud (ACC), ReCap, Inventor and Twinmotion.
Knowledge of BIM Execution Plans, ISO 19650, model coordination and digital information management.
Experience using Procore or similar project collaboration platforms.
Strong communication, organisational and problem-solving skills.
Professional proficiency in English; Spanish language skills are highly desirable.
What's on Offer
Salary of €60,000–€70,000, depending on experience.
Clear career progression within a growing international engineering business.
Exposure to complex engineering projects across multiple sectors.
Ongoing training and professional development opportunities.
A collaborative working environment with multidisciplinary teams.
The opportunity to contribute to digital engineering initiatives and continuous improvement.
What's Next
Apply now by clicking the “Apply Now” button or contact Shane Dunney at Sigmar Recruitment for more information sdunney@sigmar.ie

PepsiCo is on the look-out for a Global Operational Technology Engineer to join our global engineering function.
We are the concentrate business in PepsiCo (PGCS) working across the Beverage, Nutrition and Snacks categories to deliver concentrate for many of PepsiCo’s mega brands including Gatorade, 7Up and Pepsi. We are at the heart of PepsiCo products consumed everywhere in the world, spanning globally sourcing ingredients to manufacturing and distributing across the globe PGCS is a multi-functional business unit offering careers in various functions from Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Procurement, Quality, Finance, Tax, Customs & Trade, R&D, HR and IT. The Technical Function is our team of enabling experts offering knowledge and partnership to functions on specialist subjects including engineering, quality and productivity. They ensure operations and food safety excellence for our team. Could you bring a new dimension to our technical expertise? If so we could take your talents to a whole new level.

Outstanding communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to connect authentically, challenge assumptions constructively, and influence cross-functional partners.

Experience presenting financial strategy directly to senior operational directors and business unit heads.

The Façade Supervisor will lead the onsite construction of the Brick façade. The role will act as the primary contact and coordinator for the Bricklayers, Brickwork accessories installers, Window installers, scaffolders, fire barrier installers etc. The Façade Supervisor will be working closely with the Site Manager, Site Engineers and Project Manager. Key Responsibilities
Lead, supervise and coordinate bricklaying operatives and subcontractors to ensure works are completed safely, efficiently and in line with project programmes.
Plan daily and weekly activities, allocating labour, materials and equipment to maximise productivity and meet construction milestones.
Review drawings, specifications and construction details to ensure masonry works are delivered in accordance with design requirements.
Monitor workmanship standards and carry out regular quality inspections to ensure all brickwork, blockwork and masonry installations meet company and client expectations.

Maintain accurate site records including labour returns, progress reports, quality inspections and site instructions.
Assist with the training, mentoring and development of bricklaying operatives and apprentices, promoting best practice and continuous improvement.
Support project handover activities, ensuring snagging items are completed promptly and all masonry works are delivered to the required standards.
Requirements
Proven experience as a Bricklaying Foreman, Lead Bricklayer or similar supervisory role on residential, commercial, industrial or large-scale construction projects.
Extensive practical knowledge of brickwork, blockwork, masonry construction techniques and associated construction processes.
Strong ability to interpret construction drawings, specifications and technical details.
Demonstrated experience managing site labour, subcontractors and material resources to achieve programme targets.
Sound understanding of quality control procedures and workmanship standards within masonry construction.
Excellent leadership and communication skills, with the ability to motivate teams and build strong working relationships with site management, clients and subcontractors.
Strong organisational and problem-solving skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced construction environment.
Good understanding of health & safety legislation, safe systems of work and site compliance requirements.
Competent in the use of Microsoft Word, Excel and Outlook; experience using digital site reporting and project management systems is desirable.
Relevant trade qualification in Bricklaying or Masonry Construction. SSSTS, SMSTS or equivalent site supervisory qualification would be advantageous.
Full driving licence and willingness to travel between project locations as required.

A competitive and attractive rewards package, including pension scheme, professional subscription support and additional company benefits.
Opportunities for professional development, training and long-term career progression within the company.

Logitech is the Sweet Spot for people who want their actions to have a positive global impact while having the flexibility to do it in their own way.
Global Payroll Senior Analyst
Position Summary:
Department: Controllership Finance – Global Payroll Team
Location: Cork, Ireland - On site 2 days a week
Contract Type: Full Time / Permanent
Region Coverage: AMR
About the Role:
As an integral member of Logitech Finance, you will work in a fast-paced, dynamic Global Payroll team processing payrolls across the Americas region — covering the United States, Canada, and Latin America. You will play a key role in ensuring accurate, compliant, and timely payroll delivery, while helping to drive continuous improvement across our payroll operations.
Your Contribution:
Be Yourself. Be Open. Stay Hungry and Humble. Collaborate. Challenge. Decide and Do.
In this role you will:
Ensure the accurate and timely processing of Logitech’s end-to-end payroll for the AMR region (USA, Canada, and LATAM).
Collaborate with payroll partners to collect and validate all payroll inputs, including salaries, bonuses, benefits, allowances, and deductions. Conduct rigorous pre- and post-payroll reconciliations to eliminate anomalies or duplicate records before finalization.
Ensure the accurate and timely completion of payroll fiscal close procedures, including journal entries and balance sheet reconciliations. Work with the broader Finance team to identify and resolve payroll accounting exceptions.
Understand the full payroll cycle through to GL bookings and present meaningful flux analysis to stakeholders.
Stay current on and ensure strict compliance with federal, state/provincial, and local payroll regulations, tax laws, social security, and benefits requirements across all AMR jurisdictions.
Ensure compliance with payroll internal controls, maintaining robust documentation and proactively identifying and remediating any control gaps or weaknesses. Assist in facilitating internal and external audit engagements.
Partner with key stakeholders including People Services, HRIS, Compensation & Benefits, Stock Admin, and Finance to troubleshoot issues and work collaboratively to develop optimum processes and service delivery.
Drive the payroll Global Finance Transformation roadmap, focusing on eliminating manual workflows and implementing scalable, automated payroll solutions.
Collaborate with internal and external partners to drive automation and enhance service delivery.
Your Skills & Experience:
Beyond core technical payroll knowledge, we are seeking an innovative, highly data-literate payroll professional who actively identifies opportunities to leverage modern tools, AI, and emerging technologies to automate workflows and transform end-to-end payroll operations.
For consideration, you must bring the following skills, experience and behaviours to our team:
Experience: 3+ years of proven experience in a senior analyst payroll role, specifically working with Americas payroll (US required; Canada and LATAM experience is a major plus).
Education & Certification: Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, or a related field—or an equivalent payroll certification.
Regulatory Compliance: Solid understanding of US/Canadian payroll taxes, statutory deductions, and labour regulations.
Hands-on experience processing payroll and running reports in Workday and/or Dayforce (Ceridian).
Spreadsheet Skills: Advanced proficiency in MS Excel and Google Sheets (must be comfortable using Pivot Tables, VLOOKUP/XLOOKUP, and managing large data sets).
Familiarity with how HRIS data flows into downstream payroll and Finance/GL systems.
Strong ability to perform pre- and post-payroll reconciliations, investigate gross-to-net variances, and flag data errors before finalization.
Experience supporting month-end close procedures, including preparing journal entries and assisting Finance/FP&A teams with cost analysis.
Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills to partner effectively across HR, Finance, and external vendors.
Ability to stay organized and solve problems independently in a fast-paced, global team environment.
Customer service focus with the ability and sound judgment to handle highly sensitive information.
Process improvement mindset: have a passion for reengineering payroll processes in implementing a first-class payroll service.
Strong interest in applying emerging technologies—such as AI, ML, and RPA—to re-engineer enterprise payroll workflows, eliminate manual touchpoints, and unlock value-added insights for workforce planning.
About Logitech
With a fast-moving, innovative culture and a strong balance sheet, Logitech is a world leader in products that connect people to the digital experiences they care most about. Video conferencing, remote work, content creation, and gaming are long-term secular trends driving our business — and today all of them have accelerated, making Logitech more relevant to customers than ever.
Logitech is the sweet spot for people who are passionate about products, making a mark, and having fun doing it. We're small and flexible enough for every person to take initiative — and big enough for those actions to have a global impact.
Across Logitech we empower collaboration and foster play. We help teams collaborate/learn from anywhere, without compromising on productivity or continuity so it should be no surprise that most of our jobs are open to work from home from most locations. Our hybrid work model allows some employees to work remotely while others work on-premises. Within this structure, you may have teams or departments split between working remotely and working in-house.
Logitech is an amazing place to work because it is full of authentic people who are inclusive by nature as well as by design. Being a global company, we value our diversity and celebrate all our differences. Don’t meet every single requirement? Not a problem. If you feel you are the right candidate for the opportunity, we strongly recommend that you apply. We want to meet you!
We offer comprehensive and competitive benefits packages and working environments that are designed to be flexible and help you to care for yourself and your loved ones, now and in the future. We believe that good health means more than getting medical care when you need it. Logitech supports a culture that encourages individuals to achieve good physical, financial, emotional, intellectual and social wellbeing so we all can create, achieve and enjoy more and support our families. Working within a multidisciplinary team, you will collaborate with engineers, environmental specialists, and project managers, gaining broad project experience and exposure to clients and stakeholders. This role offers a strong platform to develop your technical skills and grow your career within Ireland’s water sector.
YOUR IMPACT
In this role, you will contribute to the delivery of essential water and wastewater infrastructure that supports communities, public health, and environmental protection across Ireland. Your work will help ensure reliable water services, improve network performance, and enhance resilience to climate change.
By applying sound engineering principles and attention to detail, you will support the development of practical, efficient, and sustainable design solutions. Your input will help projects meet regulatory requirements, reduce environmental impact, and deliver long-term value for clients and stakeholders.
Through collaboration with multidisciplinary teams, you will play a part in driving high-quality project outcomes, strengthening client relationships, and supporting the continued growth and reputation of Stantec in Ireland’s water sector.
About You
You are a qualified Civil Engineer with a strong technical foundation and proven experience in water network design. You bring a practical, solutions-focused mindset and are comfortable working both independently and as part of a collaborative, multidisciplinary team.
You Will Demonstrate
A minimum Level 8 degree in Engineering (or a related discipline)
Strong post-graduate experience in water network design
Solid professional and technical knowledge, with the ability to apply engineering principles effectively
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to engage with colleagues and clients
WHY JOIN US
We put people first: We're proud of our friendly, inclusive and collaborative environment where everyone feels valued and driven to succeed.
We are driven to achieve: Named in the top 50 companies to work by Glassdoor 2025. Recognised by Corporate Knights as one of the world's top 10 most sustainable companies 2025. =

We are better together: A supportive and collaborative team environment to assist with the growth of your career.
Growth: We're on an exciting growth journey across the Ireland - we want you to be part of it!
Great Benefits: Competitive salary, enhanced pension plan, annual leave with the option to buy/sell additional days, private medical insurance, group income protection & life assurance included as standard!
About Stantec
Whether you’re starting out on your engineering career or are looking for a fresh challenge, Ryan Hanley, now part of Stantec, is a great career move.
Based in Dublin, Galway, Castlebar and Cork, we are actively recruiting for team players with experience in any of the following areas – water and wastewater treatment process and network design, integrated network management, structural design, site development, road and bridge engineering, project management and administration.
You’ll be working for a dynamic company with an excellent reputation in the industry.

jobs.title: Design Manager (Design & Build)
jobs.desc:
At Jacobs, we're challenging today to reinvent tomorrow by solving the world's most critical problems for thriving cities, resilient environments, mission-critical outcomes, operational advancement, scientific discovery and cutting-edge manufacturing, turning abstract ideas into realities that transform the world for good.
Your impact
You will help turn some of the UK & Ireland's most important water and wastewater plans into safe, buildable and effective infrastructure.
Working across multidisciplinary programmes, you will bring engineering disciplines, construction teams and client stakeholders together around clear, coordinated design decisions. You will help identify risks early, improve buildability and make sure commissioning, operational performance and whole-life value are considered throughout the design process.
This is a role for an experienced engineering professional who understands how complex designs move from development into delivery. You will coordinate technical interfaces, manage design information and help project teams resolve issues before they affect construction, programme or cost.
You will work closely with project managers, technical specialists and construction teams, providing design management support and giving clients confidence that designs are coordinated, assured and ready for delivery.
Your contribution will go beyond managing drawings and schedules. You will challenge assumptions, support better ways of working and help teams make practical decisions that improve safety, value and long-term performance.
About The Opportunity
The UK water sector is entering a significant period of investment, creating the opportunity to improve the resilience, capacity and environmental performance of critical infrastructure.
As a Design Manager, you will coordinate multidisciplinary detailed design activities across water and wastewater projects and programmes. You will work with civil, structural, mechanical, electrical, process and construction teams to produce integrated, buildable designs that support successful delivery, commissioning and operation.
You will take day-to-day responsibility for defined design packages or project workstreams, helping manage scope, programme, technical interfaces, assurance requirements and design change. Working alongside senior design managers, project managers and discipline leads, you will track progress, coordinate inputs and help resolve technical or delivery issues.
You will also work closely with construction and commissioning teams to make sure buildability, sequencing, access, safety and operational requirements are reflected in the design. Where opportunities exist, you will support the use of standardised solutions, digital tools and lessons learned to improve design efficiency and consistency.
Depending on the size and complexity of the programme, you may coordinate a small design team or manage several technical packages within a larger multidisciplinary delivery environment. You will provide clear direction and constructive support, but you will not be expected to carry the same practice leadership, business development or people-management responsibilities as a Senior Design Manager.
This is a great opportunity to join a growing water practice and take on greater responsibility across complex infrastructure programmes. Success will mean improving design coordination, identifying risk early and helping multidisciplinary teams produce engineering solutions that work in design, construction and operation.
This role can be based out of several locations across our major UK & Ireland offices
Here's what you'll need
We would be delighted to hear from and speak to candidates with a progressive mix of the following
Experience coordinating the design or engineering delivery of water, wastewater or comparable infrastructure projects within a consultancy, contractor, delivery partner or asset-owner environment.
Evidence of managing defined design packages or project workstreams, including design scope, programme, technical interfaces, deliverables, assurance activities and change.
Practical understanding of how engineering design interacts with construction, commissioning, operations and maintenance
Working knowledge of Design & Build contracts and CDM requirements, helping teams identify, record and manage design risk.
Experience working within NEC3 or NEC4 delivery environments, including an understanding of change control, early warnings and the relationship between design decisions, programme and cost.
We offer
Competitive salary We offer compensation that reflects your skills and experience
Flexible Work Arrangements Benefit from hybrid, part-time, and flexible working hours, patterns, and locations
Robust Pension Contributions We offer enhanced pension contributions up to 10% to secure your future
Comprehensive Health Coverage Single medical cover and Digital GP service, with options to add your partner and family
Family Planning Support Access to fertility healthcare and family planning services
Enhanced Parental Leave Enjoy enhanced parental leave pay and free membership to employee assistance and parental programs
Life assurance at 4x your salary
Wellbeing Hub Free access to wellbeing apps like Calm and Daily Burn
Professional Development We cover professional membership fees and provide continuous professional development (CPD) opportunities
Community Engagement Participate in charity matched-funding, paid volunteering time, and charitable donations
#Design #Water #Infrastructure

We put people at the heart of our business, and we truly believe that by supporting one another through our culture of caring, we all succeed. We value positive mental health and a sense of belonging for all employees.
With safety and flexibility always top of mind, we’ve gone beyond traditional ways of working so you have the support, means and space to maximize your potential. You’ll uncover flexible working arrangements, benefits, and opportunities, from well-being benefits to our global giving and volunteering program, to exploring new and inventive ways to help our clients make the world a better place. No matter what drives you, you’ll discover how you can cultivate, nurture, and achieve your goals – all at a single global company. Find out more about life at Jacobs.

jobs.desc:
About the role
At Tesco, we see the value in you –and right now we are hiring Customer Delivery Drivers to join our team
Our core purpose is to serve Irish shoppers a little better every day and being a
Customer Delivery Driver
you are the first face our customers see.
Being a Customer Delivery Driver is hands on, physical and full of variety. No two shifts are ever the same – customer’s look for help in all kinds of different ways.
For most of the day you’ll feel like your own boss, delivering to your customers but with a team of managers and colleagues back at base ready to support you when you need them.
Shift Pattern:
Various shifts available
You will be responsible for
Providing an excellent home shopping experience by putting our customers at the heart of everything we do is our main responsibility.
Loading the van where required, and check your van for roadworthines
Understanding the schedule and route that has been calculated for you
Looking the part in your uniform, ready to help our customers
Driving safely, responsibly and within the law
To be courteous to all road users
Serving your customer with a smile and greet them by name
Taking care of your customer’s deliveries as if they were your own
You will need
To have had a full IRISH or EU driving licence (manual or automatic) for at least 2 years with no more than 3 penalty points
To be a safe and courteous drivers
To enjoy helping others
To be personable with a good sense of humour and excellent communication skills
The ability to take the initiative and use common sense
To care about making a difference for customers and colleagues
The ability to stay calm under pressure
Please be aware that as part of our recruitment process, job offers are subject to the Garda Vetting Process and you will need to provide proof of current penalty points on your licence at Assessment Stage. This can be requested from the National Driver Licence Services (NDLS) on
1890 41 61 41. Press Option 4 and quote your driver number.
We are sorry but if you have been disqualified from driving within the last 10 years, we will not be able to accept your application.
Should you be successful in your application, your offer will be subject to and conditional upon you providing your bank account details before your agreed start date.
Whats in it for you?
We offer excellent benefits that help make Tesco a great place to work. These include but aren’t limited to:
A variety of shifts
Part time and full time contracts available between 20 -  39 hours   a week
An hourly rate of pay for new drivers of €18.24 per hour with additional premium for Sunday working
Annual Bonus Scheme
Colleague Clubcard offering 10% discount across stores and online, with 15% discount weekends once a month (Friday to Sunday), and 20% off twice a year. There is also 20% off F&F clothing, all year long, these various discounts can be extended to a family member with a 2
nd
Clubcard available.*
Our Virtual GP service provides free and confidential access to an online GP through video GP consultations, and online prescription service for colleagues. The service is also available to families of colleagues who live at the same address for a reduced cost.
24/7 access to our Employee Assistance Programme (EAP) for you and family members for in the moment emotional support along with free access to a range of wellbeing services supporting you under our new Wellbeing First approach of Body, Mind and Life.
Life Assurance
Pension Plan*
Save As You Earn Scheme*
Paid Family Leave
Bike to Work
Long Service Awards
Commuter Scheme
*Entry requirements and rules of the scheme apply
About Us
Our vision at Tesco is to become every customer’s favourite way to shop, whether they are at home or out on the move.  Our core purpose is “Serving our customers, communities and planet a little better every day”.  Serving means more than a transactional relationship with our customers.  It means acting as a responsible and sustainable business for all stakeholders, for the communities we are part of, and for the planet. Through initiatives like the Tesco Community Fund, our association with Children’s Health Foundation, our partnership with FoodCloud and our Stronger Starts programme, we have supported over 21,000 community groups, raised over €7.5 million for medical equipment, and provided almost 15 million meals nationwide, to those living in food insecurity.
Tesco has operated in the Irish retail market since 1997, and with 190+ stores nationwide, we employ over 13,000 people in cities and towns around Ireland, supporting almost 45,000 jobs directly and indirectly. We partner with over 500 Irish suppliers - of which almost three-quarters are small and medium enterprises - which in turn supports almost 13,000 farming families around Ireland. Tesco is the single largest buyer of Irish food and drink in the world, buying €1.6 Billion a year; more than any other single country in the European Union, more than even the USA which you perceive as a massive buyer of Irish food.
We work closely with suppliers across Ireland who are dedicated to making the best products for our customers and this is reflected in the numerous awards our products have won over the years including Blás Na hÉireann, World Steak Challenge and Great Taste Awards.
We are proud to have an inclusive culture at Tesco where everyone truly feels able to be themselves. It is embedded in our values: we treat people how they want to be treated.   At Tesco, we not only celebrate diversity, but recognise the value and opportunity it brings.  We always want our colleagues to feel they can be themselves at work and we are committed to helping them be at their best.
We know life looks a little different for each of us. That’s why at Tesco, we always welcome chats about flexible working. Others are going through life-changing moments like becoming a carer, nearing retirement, adapting to parenthood, or something else.
